note.note:
History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
Young woman with 2-day history of central lower-abdominal pain, urinary frequency, and pink-tinged urine was assessed remotely; uncomplicated lower urinary-tract infection felt most likely and oral antibiotics for 3 days were prescribed with safety-net advice.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Pain in my lower tummy” for the past 2 days.  
• Location: central/suprapubic.  
• Character/severity: not further characterized.  
• Associated symptoms:
  – Feels hot/sweaty; home temperature 37 °C one hour prior.  
  – Mild nausea; no vomiting.  
  – Slight pink discoloration of urine noted once (gross hematuria).  
  – Increased urinary frequency; denies dysuria; no foul odor.  
  – Increased thirst.  
  – Constipation last week; bowel movement normal two hours before call; no diarrhoea, no blood in stool.  
  – No flank/back pain, no upper-abdominal pain or reflux, no vaginal discharge, no inter-menstrual or post-coital bleeding, no shivering/rigors.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: none reported.  
• Prior episodes: none.  
• Travel: no recent travel.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic illnesses reported.  
• Surgical/obstetric/gynecologic: contraceptive implant removed 1 year ago; menses regular.  
• No other significant history.

Medications:
• No regular prescription or OTC medications.  
• Planned: 3-day course of oral antibiotics (drug/dose/route/frequency not documented).  
Allergies:
• Amoxicillin – reaction details not described.

Social History:
• Lives with parents.  
• Smoking: non-smoker.  
• Alcohol: ~1 beer on 4 days/week.  
• Occupation and recreational drug use: not discussed.

Family History:
• Mother had early-stage breast cancer, treated successfully.  
• No other familial conditions mentioned.

Physical Examination:
Vitals: patient-reported temperature 37 °C; other vitals not provided.  
Examination findings: Not recorded (remote consultation).

Investigations:
• None performed or ordered during this visit.

Assessment & Plan:

Overall Impression:
Most consistent with acute uncomplicated cystitis; other considerations include urolithiasis and early appendicitis.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Acute uncomplicated cystitis – suprapubic pain, frequency, visible hematuria, minimal systemic signs; fits presentation.  
2. Urolithiasis – hematuria and nausea supportive; absence of colicky flank pain argues against but still possible.  
3. Early appendicitis – central abdominal pain/nausea supportive; urinary features make it less likely.

Issue 1: Suspected acute uncomplicated urinary-tract infection  
Assessment: New suprapubic pain, frequency, hematuria without systemic illness or flank pain.  
Plan:  
• Prescribed 3-day course of oral antibiotic (twice daily; specific drug/dose not documented).  
• Educated regarding red-flag symptoms: increasing pain, high fever, new back/flank pain, persisting or worsening symptoms, or recurrence.  
• Advised to seek face-to-face review if red-flag symptoms occur.  
• Prescription sent to patient’s nominated pharmacy.

Issue 2: Gross hematuria (single episode)  
Assessment: Likely inflammatory secondary to cystitis but needs monitoring.  
Plan:  
• Reassure; expected to resolve with treatment.  
• If hematuria persists after completion of antibiotics, arrange urine culture, urinalysis, and consider renal/bladder ultrasound.  

Issue 3: General health maintenance  
Plan:  
• Review allergy history if alternative antibiotics required (amoxicillin allergy).  
• Encourage adequate hydration.  
• Alcohol within recommended limits; continue avoidance of smoking.  
• No immediate need for further screening; routine primary-care follow-up as required.

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected: pregnancy status not ascertained; no urinalysis or culture performed; vital signs other than temperature not documented.  
• Conflicts: none noted between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: clear audio; occasional conversational interruptions but clinically adequate.
